precepts.text: Dinah was not raped. She went out to see the daughters of the land on her own, away from her father and twelve brothers who surely brought the wisdom pertaining to a woman to her; if thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly. Shechem saw she was not rolling in the spirit of her fathers and took her, and his soul clave unto her, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel. That is the part: you gave him your ear, he got your underwear. She was enticed, beguiled, allured away from her protection. Slick brothers read your spirit when you are not studying and hit you in the DM. Her brothers said you are not keeping her, so she had to live with the stain; you read nothing of her after that.
precepts.point: Whoremongering brothers come in, fake the funk, become soldiers, and slip into the sisters' DMs. That is why we tell you to exchange medical records and check for what needs checking when you correctly come together; we do not need to see them, you show each other. These brothers look for spinsters, sisters with the anxieties of getting too old and not being married yet, and gas them up; all bread is sweet to a whoremonger.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
Christ says, “except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” We claim we want the days shortened, but we are not ready, because wicked brothers are trying to slide in. Brothers and sisters who come from the world with a world mentality would love nothing more than to seduce and defile you, men and women both, because they don't want to change. Negroes don't like change. They pretend they've changed and put on the fringes and the border of blue so you let your guard down, then work behind the scenes to allure you away from your protection.

Dinah shows how it happens, and she was not raped. “And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.” Was she snatched? No, she went out on her own. With a father and twelve mighty brothers, you know they brought her the wisdom that pertains to a woman, and tried to keep her in straitly, the way the scripture says to keep a shameless daughter. She did not want to hear it. She wandered away from her father and her brethren.

“And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” Something in her spirit let him know. He knew whose daughter she was, and he saw she was not rolling in the spirit of her fathers or her brethren. That is how slick brothers hit sisters in the DMs: they read your spirit when you are not studying, and once they talk that talk, you feed right into it.

“And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.” That is the part that tells you it was not rape: he spake kindly to her. You gave him your ear, he got your underwear. She was enticed, beguiled, allured: drawn away from her protection, from her fathers, from how she was raised, from the protections leadership put around her. Enticing is covetousness; she belonged to Jacob, and he drew her away. Then he asked to marry her, and her brothers said no, you already defiled her. She had to live with that stain for wandering out of her father’s care, and you read nothing of her after that.

Christ warns, “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect”: some of you men and women of the third slated to make it. Everybody with fringes and a border of blue is not right; do not look at his pretty beard. One who tells women marriage is not the goal and singleness is not the curse, while flaunting his own wife, is the devil in black flesh; he wants the women to stay in sin. A woman in the world turned down one of these street preachers when he broke character to ask for her number. A woman in the world knows more about the commandments than a negro with fringes and a Bible who is supposed to be keeping them, yet a sister in here will entertain the same kind in her DMs. Whoremongering brothers fake the funk, become soldiers, and look for spinsters, sisters anxious about getting older and not married yet, and gas them up, because all bread is sweet to a whoremonger. That is why, when you correctly come together, you exchange medical records and show each other; leadership does not need to see them. Give diligence and study, so you can recognize deception at your door, whatever it is wearing.

precepts.text: Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.
precepts.point: The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters. Have a care of their body; do not give overmuch liberty; the father wakes for the daughter and the care for her takes away sleep. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
“Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.”

Dinah, Jacob's only daughter, “went out to see the daughters of the land” without supervision, and Shechem “took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” This was stranger rape. The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters and have a care of their body. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

precepts.text: If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.
precepts.point: The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters. Have a care of their body; do not give overmuch liberty; the father wakes for the daughter and the care for her takes away sleep. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

Dinah went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem took her and defiled her. Do not give overmuch liberty. Keep the daughters in straitly; everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

precepts.text: The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth; keep a sure watch, lest she be defiled and made a reproach.
precepts.point: The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters. Have a care of their body; do not give overmuch liberty; the father wakes for the daughter and the care for her takes away sleep. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
“The father waketh for the daughter, when no man knoweth; and the care for her taketh away sleep”: when she is young, “In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house”, and when she is married, lest she misbehave or be barren. “Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people”.

That is the charge Dinah's story presses. She went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem the son of Hamor “took her, and lay with her, and defiled her”: stranger rape, and a reproach on the house of Jacob. The father wakes for the daughter, and the care for her takes away sleep: keep a sure watch, so that she is not defiled. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

precepts.text: O Lord God of my father Simeon, to whom thou gavest a sword to take vengeance of the strangers who defiled the maid; the vengeance was ordained of God, and they were moved with His zeal.
precepts.point: Two men do not take a city alone. The sword of Simeon was given of God to take vengeance of the strangers that defiled the maid; they were moved with the zeal of the Most High, and He was behind the judgment.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
Judith prays, “O Lord God of my father Simeon, to whom thou gavest a sword to take vengeance of the strangers, who loosened the girdle of a maid to defile her, and discovered the thigh to her shame, and polluted her virginity to her reproach; for thou saidst, It shall not be so; and yet they did so”. The Most High gave their rulers to be slain, “and smotest the servants with their lords, and the lords upon their thrones”, and gave “their wives for a prey, and their daughters to be captives, and all their spoils to be divided among thy dear children; which were moved with thy zeal”.

That is Genesis 34 told from heaven's side. Two men do not take a city alone; Simeon and Levi came upon the city boldly and slew all the males, slew Hamor and Shechem, took Dinah out, spoiled the city and carried away the wives and little ones and all the wealth, exactly as Judith recounts. The sword of Simeon was given of God to take vengeance of the strangers that defiled the maid. They were moved with the zeal of the Most High, and He was behind the judgment.

precepts.text: There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel; the answer of Simeon and Levi stood on that law.
precepts.point: The brothers answered, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot? There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel; the daughters of Israel are not to be handled so, and the sons of Israel did not go for it.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
“There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.”

Jacob was troubled, fearing the nations round about would gather against his house, few in number as it was. The brothers answered him, “Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?” Their answer stood on that law: the daughters of Israel are not to be handled so, and the sons of Israel did not go for it.

precepts.text: The men of Shechem were circumcised, and on the third day, when they were sore, Simeon and Levi slew all the males; that is the anger Jacob cursed.
precepts.point: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel: Levi had no whole portion but cities scattered throughout all the tribes; and as Judah was scattered to the four corners of the earth, so was Levi, for Judah, Benjamin, and Levi make up the southern kingdom.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised.” Then “on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.”

That is “in their anger they slew a man.” When their sister was defiled at Shechem, they told all the men of the city to be circumcised, and while the men were sore they slew every male of the city. Simeon and Levi did not play. That is the anger Jacob cursed: “Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel.”

Simeon is the so-called Dominican and Levi the so-called Haitian today, brethren sharing the same island, Hispaniola, and still divided in Jacob and scattered in Israel.

precepts.text: Shechem offered never so much dowry and gift for Dinah; the dowry stood even where the union was wrong.
precepts.point: The dowry of virgins was fifty shekels of silver, paid by the man who laid hold on a damsel not betrothed, and she became his wife whom he could not put away all his days. And if a husband afterward brought up an evil name upon a virgin of Israel, saying he found her not a maid, the tokens of her virginity, the cloth from the bedchamber her father kept, were spread before the elders; the man was chastised and amerced in an hundred shekels of silver for the false report.

note.label: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution

precepts.why:
“If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” The father does not agree with the backdoor marriage, and the man still pays. Genesis 34 gives the example with Dinah: “And Shechem said unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find grace in your eyes, and what ye shall say unto me I will give. Ask me never so much dowry and gift, and I will give according as ye shall say unto me: but give me the damsel to wife.”

Shechem and his father Hamor begged Jacob for her and offered never so much dowry. Shechem understood the union was not supposed to take place, the Hebrews with the Hamites, and the dowry stood even where the union was wrong.
